context: 5-stage Sankey diagram tracing U.S. energy flow from 6 primary sources (coal, gas, nuclear, solar, wind, hydro) through 2 generation nodes, 2 grid nodes, 4 demand sectors, to 6 end uses, with 3 loss nodes highlighted separately — 21 nodes, ~33 links, 5 stage colors plus a distinct red for losses
first_impression: Reads cleanly at a glance — the left-to-right stage structure is immediately legible and the red dashed loss flows stand out without dominating.
what_works: Stage color coding (Tol muted palette, 5+1 hues) gives each column a distinct identity so the eye can anchor to a stage before tracing individual flows; gradient links that shift from source to target color reinforce directionality and reduce ambiguity at crossings. Loss flows are doubly encoded (red + dashed stroke) making them immediately identifiable without a legend lookup.
what_doesnt: The Grid-to-Sectors crossing zone is the densest area — High-Voltage Transmission fans out to all four sectors while Local Distribution does the same, producing overlapping arcs that are hard to untangle without hovering; the bottom cluster where Generation Losses, Transmission Losses, and Distribution Losses all converge spatially amplifies this local tangle. Hover-based path highlighting is the intended remedy but perceptual quality of that interaction cannot be assessed from a static screenshot.
